title: Extractor Functions
text: Functions to extract specific components from fitted bgms and bgmCompare objects.

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_arguments
Retrieve the arguments used when fitting a model with bgm() or bgmCompare().
extract_arguments(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms or bgmCompare object.



Returns a named list containing all arguments passed to the fitting function, including data dimensions, prior settings, and MCMC configuration.

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_main_effects
Retrieve posterior mean main-effect parameters.
extract_main_effects(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms or bgmCompare object.



The structure depends on the model type:

GGM (bgms): NULL. GGM models have no main effects; the precision matrix diagonal is on coef(fit)$pairwise.
OMRF (bgms): A numeric matrix (p x max_categories) of posterior mean category thresholds. Columns beyond the number of categories for a variable are NA.
Mixed MRF (bgms): A list with $discrete (threshold matrix) and $continuous (means matrix).
bgmCompare: A matrix with one row per post-warmup iteration, containing posterior samples of baseline main-effect parameters.

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_pairwise_interactions
Retrieve posterior samples of pairwise interaction parameters.
extract_pairwise_interactions(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms or bgmCompare object.



Returns a matrix with one row per post-warmup iteration and one column per edge. For bgmCompare, columns correspond to baseline pairwise interaction parameters.

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_indicators
Retrieve posterior samples of inclusion indicators.
extract_indicators(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms or bgmCompare object.



Returns a matrix with one row per post-warmup iteration and one column per indicator, containing binary (0/1) samples:

bgms: One column per edge. Requires edge_selection = TRUE.
bgmCompare: Columns for main-effect and pairwise difference indicators. Requires difference_selection = TRUE.

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_posterior_inclusion_probabilities
Compute posterior inclusion probabilities.
extract_posterior_inclusion_probabilities(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms or bgmCompare object.



Returns a symmetric p x p matrix of posterior inclusion probabilities:

bgms: Off-diagonal entries are edge inclusion probabilities. Requires edge_selection = TRUE.
bgmCompare: Diagonal entries are main-effect inclusion probabilities; off-diagonal entries are pairwise difference inclusion probabilities. Requires difference_selection = TRUE.

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_indicator_priors
Retrieve the prior specification used for inclusion indicators.
extract_indicator_priors(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms or bgmCompare object.



Returns a named list describing the prior structure, including the prior type and hyperparameters:

bgms: Requires edge_selection = TRUE. Returns the prior type ("Bernoulli", "Beta-Bernoulli", or "Stochastic-Block") and associated hyperparameters.
bgmCompare: Requires difference_selection = TRUE. Returns the difference prior specification.

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_group_params
Compute group-specific parameter estimates by combining baseline parameters and group differences.
extract_group_params(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgmCompare object.



Returns a list with main_effects_groups (main effects per group) and pairwise_effects_groups (pairwise effects per group).

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_sbm
Retrieve posterior summaries from a model fitted with the Stochastic Block prior.
extract_sbm(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms object.



Requires edge_selection = TRUE and edge_prior = "Stochastic-Block". Returns a list with:

posterior_num_blocks — Posterior probabilities for each possible number of clusters.
posterior_mean_allocations — Posterior mean cluster allocations.
posterior_mode_allocations — Posterior mode cluster allocations.
posterior_mean_coclustering_matrix — Co-clustering proportion matrix.

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_ess
Retrieve effective sample size estimates for all parameters.
extract_ess(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms or bgmCompare object.



Returns a named list with ESS values for each parameter type present in the model (e.g., main, pairwise, indicator).

title: Extractor Functions
text:
extract_rhat
Retrieve R-hat convergence diagnostics for all parameters.
extract_rhat(bgms_object)



Argument
Description




bgms_object
A fitted bgms or bgmCompare object.



Returns a named list with R-hat values for each parameter type present in the model (e.g., main, pairwise, indicator).

title: S3 Methods
text:
coef
Extract posterior mean coefficients.

bgms
coef(object, ...)



Argument
Description




object
An object of class bgms.


...
Ignored.



Returns a list with:

main — Posterior mean main-effect parameters. NULL for GGM models. For OMRF models: a numeric matrix (p x max_categories) of category thresholds. For mixed MRF models: a list with $discrete (threshold matrix) and $continuous (means matrix).
pairwise — Posterior mean pairwise interaction matrix. For GGM and mixed MRF models the precision matrix diagonal is included on the diagonal.
indicator — Posterior mean edge inclusion indicators (if available).



bgmCompare
coef(object, ...)



Argument
Description




object
An object of class bgmCompare.


...
Ignored.



Returns a list with:

main_effects_raw — Posterior means of raw main-effect parameters (variables x (baseline + differences)).
pairwise_effects_raw — Posterior means of raw pairwise-effect parameters (pairs x (baseline + differences)).
main_effects_groups — Posterior means of group-specific main effects (variables x groups), computed as baseline plus projected differences.
pairwise_effects_groups — Posterior means of group-specific pairwise effects (pairs x groups), computed as baseline plus projected differences.
indicators — Posterior mean inclusion probabilities as a symmetric matrix, with diagonals for main effects and off-diagonals for pairwise effects.

title: S3 Methods
text:
predict
Compute conditional probability distributions for one or more variables given the observed values of other variables in the data.

bgms
predict(object, newdata, variables = NULL,
        type = c("probabilities", "response"),
        method = c("posterior-mean", "posterior-sample"),
        ndraws = NULL, seed = NULL, ...)







Argument
Description




object
An object of class bgms.


newdata
A matrix or data frame with n rows and p columns. Must match the variables used in fitting.


variables
Character vector of names, integer vector of column indices, or NULL (all variables).


type
"probabilities" (full conditional distribution) or "response" (predicted category).


method
"posterior-mean" (use posterior means) or "posterior-sample" (average over draws).


ndraws
Number of posterior draws for "posterior-sample". NULL uses all draws.


seed
Optional random seed.



Ordinal models: For type = "probabilities", returns a named list with one matrix per variable (n rows x (num_categories + 1) columns). For type = "response", returns a matrix of predicted categories.
GGM models: For type = "probabilities", returns a list with one matrix per variable (n rows x 2 columns: "mean" and "sd"). For type = "response", returns conditional means.
Mixed MRF models: Returns a list combining both formats for discrete and continuous variables.
When method = "posterior-sample", predictions include an "sd" attribute with the standard deviation across draws.


bgmCompare
predict(object, newdata, group, variables = NULL,
        type = c("probabilities", "response"),
        method = c("posterior-mean"), ...)







Argument
Description




object
An object of class bgmCompare.


newdata
A matrix or data frame matching the original variables.


group
Integer specifying which group’s parameters to use (1 to number of groups). Required.


variables
Which variables to predict (character, integer, or NULL for all).


type
"probabilities" or "response".


method
"posterior-mean" (posterior mean parameters).



Returns the same structure as predict.bgms, using group-specific parameters obtained by combining baseline parameters and group differences.

title: S3 Methods
text:
simulate
Generate new observations from a fitted model.

bgms
simulate(object, nsim = 500, seed = NULL,
         method = c("posterior-mean", "posterior-sample"),
         ndraws = NULL, iter = 1000,
         cores = parallel::detectCores(),
         display_progress = c("per-chain", "total", "none"), ...)







Argument
Description




object
An object of class bgms.


nsim
Number of observations to simulate. Default: 500.


seed
Optional random seed.


method
"posterior-mean" (single simulation) or "posterior-sample" (one dataset per draw, parallel).


ndraws
Number of posterior draws for "posterior-sample". NULL uses all.


iter
Gibbs iterations for equilibration. Default: 1000.


cores
CPU cores for parallel execution with "posterior-sample".


display_progress
Progress bar style: "per-chain", "total", or "none".



If method = "posterior-mean": a matrix (nsim x p). If method = "posterior-sample": a list of matrices, one per posterior draw. For mixed MRF models, discrete columns contain integers and continuous columns contain real values.


bgmCompare
simulate(object, nsim = 500, seed = NULL, group,
         method = c("posterior-mean"), iter = 1000, ...)







Argument
Description




object
An object of class bgmCompare.


nsim
Number of observations to simulate. Default: 500.


seed
Optional random seed.


group
Integer specifying which group to simulate from (1 to number of groups). Required.


method
"posterior-mean".


iter
Gibbs iterations for equilibration. Default: 1000.



Returns a matrix (nsim x p) of simulated observations for the specified group.

title: S3 Methods
text:
simulate_mrf
Simulate observations from a Markov Random Field using user-specified parameters (no fitted model needed).
simulate_mrf(
  num_states,
  num_variables,
  num_categories,
  pairwise,
  main,
  variable_type = "ordinal",
  baseline_category,
  iter = 1000,
  seed = NULL
)







Argument
Description




num_states
Number of observations to generate.


num_variables
Number of variables in the MRF.


num_categories
Integer or integer vector. Number of response categories on top of the base category (1 = binary).


pairwise
Symmetric matrix of pairwise interactions. For continuous variables, this is the precision matrix (must be positive definite).


main
Main-effect parameters. For ordinal variables: a matrix of category thresholds. For continuous variables: a means vector.


variable_type
"ordinal", "blume-capel", or "continuous". Can be a vector for mixed types (ordinal/Blume-Capel only).


baseline_category
Integer vector of baseline categories for Blume–Capel variables.


iter
Gibbs iterations for equilibration (ordinal only). Default: 1000.


seed
Optional random seed.



Returns a (num_states x num_variables) matrix of simulated observations.
For ordinal and Blume-Capel variables, the Gibbs sampler generates observations from full conditional distributions. For continuous variables, observations are drawn directly from \(N(\mu, \Omega^{-1})\).

Four top-level sections, each with a distinct audience and purpose.


Teaches concepts and walks through analyses. A reader who finishes the Guide can fit models, interpret output, and set priors with confidence.

Purpose

Analyses



guide/edge-selection.qmd
Bayesian edge selection: inclusion Bayes factors, posterior inclusion probabilities. Includes analysis-specific prior guidance.


guide/group-comparison.qmd
Comparing networks across groups with bgmCompare(). Includes analysis-specific prior guidance.

Stochastic block model for edge clustering. Includes analysis-specific prior guidance.


MCMC output

What the sampler returns: posterior samples, summary statistics, raw output structure.


guide/mcmc-diagnostics.qmd
Convergence checks: ESS, R-hat, trace plots, divergences, E-BFMI.



Pedagogical flow: Background → Models → Analyses → MCMC output. Each analysis page includes a short prior section specific to that analysis, so readers learn about priors in context rather than in the abstract.



One page per exported function or function family. Content is extracted from roxygen documentation with minimal paraphrasing.







Page
Purpose

Section landing page with function index.


reference/bgm.qmd
bgm(): all arguments, defaults, return structure.

bgmCompare(): all arguments, defaults, return structure.

S3 methods: print, plot, summary, simulate, predict.

Bundled datasets.






For developers and methodologists who need to understand how bgms works under the hood. Each page explains a subsystem with reference to the actual code.







Page
Purpose




manual/index.qmd
Section landing page and subsystem map.


Architecture



manual/architecture.qmd
Top-level design: R front-end → C++ engine. The three-stage pipeline (bgm_spec → run_sampler → build_output). Package directory layout.


manual/r-scaffolding.qmd
The R layer in detail: validation pipeline (validate_data, validate_variable_types, validate_sampler), spec construction (bgm_spec, new_bgm_spec, validate_bgm_spec), sampler dispatch (run_sampler → model-specific C++ entry points), output assembly (build_output → posterior summaries, raw samples, diagnostics). Data flow diagram from user call to returned fit object.


manual/model-classes.qmd
C++ class hierarchy: BaseModel → GGMModel, OMRFModel, MixedMRFModel. Virtual interface (capability queries, parameter access, edge selection, adaptation, missing data). How models register their storage layout.


MCMC engine



manual/samplers.qmd
Sampler hierarchy: SamplerBase → MetropolisSampler, GradientSamplerBase → HMCSampler, NUTSSampler, HybridNUTSSampler. Step-size adaptation, mass matrix tuning. Factory dispatch by sampler_type string.


manual/nuts.qmd
NUTS algorithm: recursive tree-building, U-turn criterion, multinomial sampling, divergence detection. How tree depth and energy diagnostics are recorded.


manual/warmup.qmd
Three-stage adaptive warmup schedule: stage 1 (step-size), stage 2 (mass matrix), stage 3a (final step-size). Edge-selection phases 3b (proposal-SD tuning) and 3c (graph initialization). How WarmupSchedule coordinates sampler and model.


manual/parallel-chains.qmd
Parallel chain execution: model.clone() / edge_prior.clone() per chain, TBB thread control via tbb::global_control, RcppParallel::parallelFor dispatch through MCMCChainRunner. Sequential fallback for single-thread mode. Per-chain RNG seeding (config.seed + chain_id). Progress tracking and user-interrupt handling across threads.


Models



manual/ggm-internals.qmd
GGM implementation: precision matrix parameterization, Cholesky updates (cholupdate), continuous-data likelihood and gradient, edge-specific Metropolis proposals.


manual/omrf-internals.qmd
OMRF implementation: ordinal threshold parameterization, Blume-Capel model with linear + quadratic effects, pseudo-likelihood, full-conditional Gibbs steps for edge indicators.


manual/variable-helpers.qmd

title: bgm
text: Bayesian estimation or edge selection for Markov Random Fields.

title: bgm
text:
Description
The bgm function estimates the pseudoposterior distribution of the parameters of a Markov Random Field (MRF) for binary, ordinal, continuous, or mixed (discrete and continuous) variables. Depending on the variable types, the model is an ordinal MRF, a Gaussian graphical model (GGM), or a mixed MRF. Optionally, it performs Bayesian edge selection using spike-and-slab priors to infer the network structure.

title: bgm
text:
Usage
bgm(
  x,
  variable_type = "ordinal",
  baseline_category,
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 1000,
  pairwise_scale = 2.5,
  main_alpha = 0.5,
  main_beta = 0.5,
  edge_selection = TRUE,
  edge_prior = c("Bernoulli", "Beta-Bernoulli", "Stochastic-Block"),
  inclusion_probability = 0.5,
  beta_bernoulli_alpha = 1,
  beta_bernoulli_beta = 1,
  beta_bernoulli_alpha_between = 1,
  beta_bernoulli_beta_between = 1,
  dirichlet_alpha = 1,
  lambda = 1,
  na_action = c("listwise", "impute"),
  update_method = c("nuts", "adaptive-metropolis", "hamiltonian-mc"),
  target_accept,
  hmc_num_leapfrogs = 100,
  nuts_max_depth = 10,
  learn_mass_matrix = TRUE,
  chains = 4,
  cores = parallel::detectCores(),
  display_progress = c("per-chain", "total", "none"),
  seed = NULL,
  standardize = FALSE,
  pseudolikelihood = c("conditional", "marginal"),
  verbose = getOption("bgms.verbose", TRUE)
)

title: bgm
text:
Arguments

Data







Argument
Description




x
A data frame or matrix with n rows and p columns containing binary and ordinal responses. Variables are automatically recoded to non-negative integers (0, 1, ..., m). For regular ordinal variables, unobserved categories are collapsed; for Blume–Capel variables, all categories are retained.


variable_type
Character or character vector specifying the type of each variable. Allowed values: "ordinal", "blume-capel", or "continuous". A single string applies to all variables. A per-variable vector that mixes discrete ("ordinal" / "blume-capel") and "continuous" types fits a mixed MRF. Binary variables are automatically treated as "ordinal". Default: "ordinal".


baseline_category
Integer or vector. Baseline category for Blume–Capel variables. Can be a single integer (applied to all) or a vector of length p. Required if at least one variable is of type "blume-capel".


na_action
How to handle missing data: "listwise" (drop rows with missing values) or "impute" (single imputation during sampling). Default: "listwise".





Prior specification







Argument
Description




pairwise_scale
Scale of the Cauchy prior for pairwise interaction parameters. Default: 2.5.


main_alpha, main_beta
Shape parameters of the beta-prime prior for threshold parameters. Must be positive. Defaults: 0.5.


edge_selection
Logical. Whether to perform Bayesian edge selection. If FALSE, the model estimates all edges. Default: TRUE.


edge_prior
Prior for edge inclusion: "Bernoulli", "Beta-Bernoulli", or "Stochastic-Block". Default: "Bernoulli".


inclusion_probability
Prior inclusion probability of each edge (Bernoulli prior). Default: 0.5.


beta_bernoulli_alpha, beta_bernoulli_beta
Shape parameters for the beta distribution in the Beta–Bernoulli and Stochastic-Block priors. For the Stochastic-Block prior these are the within-cluster parameters. Defaults: 1.


beta_bernoulli_alpha_between, beta_bernoulli_beta_between
Shape parameters for between-cluster edge inclusion probabilities in the Stochastic-Block prior. Defaults: 1.


dirichlet_alpha
Concentration parameter of the Dirichlet prior on block assignments (Stochastic Block model). Default: 1.


lambda
Rate of the zero-truncated Poisson prior on the number of clusters (Stochastic Block model). Default: 1.


standardize
Logical. If TRUE, the Cauchy prior scale for each pairwise interaction is adjusted based on the range of response scores. Variables with more response categories have larger score products, so standardization ensures equivalent relative shrinkage across all pairs. Default: FALSE.





Sampler settings







Argument
Description




iter
Number of post-warmup iterations per chain. Default: 1000.


warmup
Number of warmup iterations before collecting samples. A minimum of 1000 is enforced. Default: 1000.


update_method
Sampling algorithm: "nuts" (No-U-Turn Sampler), "adaptive-metropolis" (componentwise Metropolis–Hastings with Robbins–Monro adaptation), or "hamiltonian-mc" (HMC with fixed path length). Default: "nuts".


target_accept
Target acceptance rate (0 to 1). Defaults: 0.44 for adaptive Metropolis, 0.65 for HMC, 0.80 for NUTS.


hmc_num_leapfrogs
Number of leapfrog steps for HMC. Default: 100.


nuts_max_depth
Maximum tree depth in NUTS. Default: 10.


learn_mass_matrix
Logical. If TRUE, adapt a diagonal mass matrix during warmup (HMC/NUTS only). Default: TRUE.


chains
Number of parallel chains. Default: 4.


cores
Number of CPU cores for parallel execution. Default: parallel::detectCores().


display_progress
Progress reporting: "per-chain", "total", or "none". Default: "per-chain".


seed
Optional integer seed for reproducibility.


pseudolikelihood
For mixed MRF models: "conditional" (conditions on continuous variables for discrete updates; faster) or "marginal" (integrates out continuous variables; more expensive). Ignored for pure ordinal or pure continuous data. Default: "conditional".


verbose
Logical. Print informational messages during data processing. Default: getOption("bgms.verbose", TRUE).

title: bgm
text:
Value
A list of class "bgms" with posterior summaries, posterior mean matrices, and access to raw MCMC draws. The object can be passed to print(), summary(), and coef().
Main components:

posterior_summary_main — Data frame with posterior summaries (mean, sd, MCSE, ESS, Rhat) for main-effect parameters. For OMRF models these are category thresholds; for mixed MRF models these are discrete thresholds and continuous means. NULL for GGM models.
posterior_summary_quadratic — Data frame with posterior summaries for the precision matrix diagonal (GGM and mixed MRF). NULL for OMRF models.
posterior_summary_pairwise — Data frame with posterior summaries for pairwise interaction parameters.
posterior_summary_indicator — Data frame with posterior summaries for edge inclusion indicators (if edge_selection = TRUE).
posterior_mean_main — Posterior mean of main-effect parameters.
posterior_mean_pairwise — Symmetric matrix of posterior mean pairwise interaction strengths. For GGM and mixed MRF models, the precision matrix diagonal is on the matrix diagonal.
posterior_mean_indicator — Symmetric matrix of posterior mean inclusion probabilities (if edge selection was enabled).
raw_samples — A list of raw MCMC draws per chain, with sublists for main, pairwise, indicator, and allocations (SBM prior).
arguments — A list of function call arguments and metadata.

Additional summaries when edge_prior = "Stochastic-Block":

posterior_summary_pairwise_allocations — Data frame with posterior summaries for pairwise cluster co-occurrence.
posterior_coclustering_matrix — Symmetric co-clustering proportion matrix.
posterior_mean_allocations — Posterior mean cluster allocations.
posterior_mode_allocations — Posterior mode cluster allocations.
posterior_num_blocks — Posterior probabilities for each possible number of clusters.

NUTS diagnostics (tree depth, divergences, energy, E-BFMI) are available in fit$nuts_diag when update_method = "nuts".

title: bgm
text:
Details

Ordinal variables
The function supports two types of ordinal variables.
Regular ordinal variables assign a category threshold parameter to each response category except the lowest. The model imposes no additional constraints on the distribution of category responses.
Blume–Capel ordinal variables assume a baseline category (e.g., a “neutral” response) and score responses by distance from this baseline. Category thresholds are modeled as:
\[\mu_c = \alpha \cdot (c - b) + \beta \cdot (c - b)^2\]
where \(\mu_c\) is the category threshold for category \(c\), \(\alpha\) is a linear trend across categories, \(\beta\) is a quadratic effect (negative values favor responses near the baseline; positive values favor extremes), and \(b\) is the baseline category.


Edge selection
When edge_selection = TRUE, the function performs Bayesian variable selection on pairwise interactions using spike-and-slab priors:

Bernoulli — Fixed inclusion probability across edges.
Beta-Bernoulli — Inclusion probability is given a Beta prior.
Stochastic-Block — Cluster-based edge priors with Beta, Dirichlet, and Poisson hyperpriors.



Prior distributions

Pairwise effects — Cauchy (slab) prior.
Main effects — Beta-prime distribution.
Edge indicators — Bernoulli, Beta-Bernoulli, or Stochastic-Block prior.



Sampling algorithms and warmup
Parameters are updated within a Gibbs framework using one of three algorithms:

Adaptive Metropolis–Hastings — Componentwise random-walk updates with Robbins–Monro proposal adaptation.
Hamiltonian Monte Carlo — Joint updates using fixed-length leapfrog trajectories. Step size is tuned during warmup via dual averaging; the diagonal mass matrix can also be adapted.
No-U-Turn Sampler — Adaptive extension of HMC with dynamically chosen trajectory lengths. Warmup uses a staged fast–slow–fast schedule.

When edge_selection = TRUE, edge-inclusion indicator updates are delayed until after the core warmup phase. The warmup schedule appends additional stages for proposal-SD tuning (Stage 3b) and graph initialization (Stage 3c), so the total warmup exceeds the user-specified value.


Missing data
If na_action = "listwise", rows with missing values are removed. If na_action = "impute", missing values are imputed within the MCMC loop via Gibbs sampling.

title: bgmCompare
text: Bayesian estimation and variable selection for group differences in Markov Random Fields.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Description
The bgmCompare function estimates group differences in category threshold parameters (main effects) and pairwise interactions (pairwise effects) of a Markov Random Field (MRF) for binary and ordinal variables. Groups can be defined either by supplying two separate datasets (x and y) or by a group membership vector. Optionally, Bayesian variable selection identifies differences across groups.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Usage
bgmCompare(
  x,
  y,
  group_indicator,
  difference_selection = TRUE,
  main_difference_selection = FALSE,
  variable_type = "ordinal",
  baseline_category,
  difference_scale = 1,
  difference_prior = c("Bernoulli", "Beta-Bernoulli"),
  difference_probability = 0.5,
  beta_bernoulli_alpha = 1,
  beta_bernoulli_beta = 1,
  pairwise_scale = 2.5,
  main_alpha = 0.5,
  main_beta = 0.5,
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 1000,
  na_action = c("listwise", "impute"),
  update_method = c("nuts", "adaptive-metropolis", "hamiltonian-mc"),
  target_accept,
  hmc_num_leapfrogs = 100,
  nuts_max_depth = 10,
  learn_mass_matrix = TRUE,
  chains = 4,
  cores = parallel::detectCores(),
  display_progress = c("per-chain", "total", "none"),
  seed = NULL,
  standardize = FALSE,
  verbose = getOption("bgms.verbose", TRUE)
)

title: bgmCompare
text:
Arguments

Data and groups







Argument
Description




x
A data frame or matrix of binary and ordinal responses for Group 1. Variables should be coded as nonnegative integers starting at 0. For ordinal variables, unused categories are collapsed; for Blume–Capel variables, all categories are retained.


y
Optional data frame or matrix for Group 2 (two-group designs). Must have the same variables (columns) as x.


group_indicator
Optional integer vector of group memberships for rows of x (multi-group designs). Ignored if y is supplied.


variable_type
Character vector specifying the type of each variable: "ordinal" (default) or "blume-capel".


baseline_category
Integer or vector giving the baseline category for Blume–Capel variables.


na_action
How to handle missing data: "listwise" (drop rows) or "impute" (impute within Gibbs). Default: "listwise".





Difference selection







Argument
Description




difference_selection
Logical. If TRUE, spike-and-slab priors are applied to difference parameters. Default: TRUE.


main_difference_selection
Logical. If TRUE, apply spike-and-slab selection to main effect (threshold) differences. Since main effects are often nuisance parameters and their selection can interfere with pairwise selection under the Beta-Bernoulli prior, the default is FALSE. Only used when difference_selection = TRUE.


difference_scale
Scale of the Cauchy prior for difference parameters. Default: 1.


difference_prior
Prior for difference inclusion: "Bernoulli" or "Beta-Bernoulli". Default: "Bernoulli".


difference_probability
Prior inclusion probability for differences (Bernoulli prior). Default: 0.5.


beta_bernoulli_alpha, beta_bernoulli_beta
Shape parameters of the Beta prior for inclusion probabilities in the Beta–Bernoulli model. Defaults: 1.





Prior specification







Argument
Description




pairwise_scale
Scale of the Cauchy prior for baseline pairwise interactions. Default: 2.5.


main_alpha, main_beta
Shape parameters of the beta-prime prior for baseline threshold parameters. Defaults: 0.5.


standardize
Logical. If TRUE, the Cauchy prior scale for each pairwise interaction (both baseline and difference) is adjusted based on the range of response scores. Default: FALSE.





Sampler settings







Argument
Description




iter
Number of post-warmup iterations per chain. Default: 1000.


warmup
Number of warmup iterations before sampling. Default: 1000.


update_method
Sampling algorithm: "nuts", "adaptive-metropolis", or "hamiltonian-mc". Default: "nuts".


target_accept
Target acceptance rate. Defaults: 0.44 (Metropolis), 0.65 (HMC), 0.80 (NUTS).


hmc_num_leapfrogs
Leapfrog steps for HMC. Default: 100.


nuts_max_depth
Maximum tree depth for NUTS. Default: 10.


learn_mass_matrix
Logical. If TRUE, adapts a diagonal mass matrix during warmup (HMC/NUTS only). Default: TRUE.


chains
Number of parallel chains. Default: 4.


cores
Number of CPU cores. Default: parallel::detectCores().


display_progress
Progress reporting: "per-chain", "total", or "none". Default: "per-chain".


seed
Optional integer seed for reproducibility.


verbose
Logical. Print informational messages during data processing. Default: getOption("bgms.verbose", TRUE).

title: bgmCompare
text:
Value
A list of class "bgmCompare" containing posterior summaries, posterior mean matrices, and raw MCMC samples:

posterior_summary_main_baseline, posterior_summary_pairwise_baseline — Summaries of baseline thresholds and pairwise interactions.
posterior_summary_main_differences, posterior_summary_pairwise_differences — Summaries of group differences in thresholds and pairwise interactions.
posterior_summary_indicator — Summaries of inclusion indicators (if difference_selection = TRUE).
posterior_mean_main_baseline, posterior_mean_pairwise_baseline — Posterior mean matrices (legacy style).
raw_samples — List of raw draws per chain for main, pairwise, and indicator parameters.
arguments — List of function call arguments and metadata.

The summary() method prints formatted summaries, and coef() extracts posterior means. NUTS diagnostics are available in fit$nuts_diag when update_method = "nuts".

title: bgmCompare
text:
Details

Pairwise interactions
For variables \(i\) and \(j\), the group-specific interaction is represented as:
\[\theta_{ij}^{(g)} = \phi_{ij} + \delta_{ij}^{(g)}\]
where \(\phi_{ij}\) is the baseline effect and \(\delta_{ij}^{(g)}\) are group differences constrained to sum to zero.


Ordinal variables
Regular ordinal variables: category thresholds are decomposed into a baseline plus group differences for each category.
Blume–Capel variables: category thresholds are quadratic in the category index, with both the linear and quadratic terms split into a baseline plus group differences.


Variable selection
When difference_selection = TRUE, spike-and-slab priors are applied to difference parameters:

Bernoulli — Fixed prior inclusion probability.
Beta-Bernoulli — Inclusion probability given a Beta prior.



Sampling algorithms and warmup
Parameters are updated within a Gibbs framework, using the same sampling algorithms and staged warmup scheme described in bgm(): adaptive Metropolis–Hastings, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, or the No-U-Turn Sampler. When difference_selection = TRUE, indicator updates are delayed until late warmup.

title: bgmCompare
text:
Examples

# Compare French and non-French groups on a subset of the Boredom data
x = Boredom[Boredom$language == "fr", 2:6]
y = Boredom[Boredom$language != "fr", 2:6]

fit = bgmCompare(x, y, chains = 2)

# Posterior inclusion probabilities
summary(fit)$indicator

# Bayesian model averaged main effects for the groups
coef(fit)$main_effects_groups

# Bayesian model averaged pairwise effects for the groups
coef(fit)$pairwise_effects_groups
